events.title: Rider Advocate brief: 7 claims (0 void)
events.body:
C1: The GPS track shows one off-route segment from 12:12 to 12:22 in which 6.47 km was driven where the optimal route covers 1.32 km, adding 5.15 km of extra distance and straying up to 1194 m from the optimal route; under RD-1 this unexplained deviation is a route deviation. [F3 F1] [RD-1]
C2: The trip was a RydeTAXI metered trip (total charged $31.56 by meter, distance $20.43 at 14.5 km), so the extra kilometres the driver drove enter the fare directly; RD-2 requires a partial refund of Σ(extra_km) × per-km rate for the non-exempt segment. [F6 F4] [RD-2]
C3: Using the fare facts for this trip, the per-kilometre rate is $1.41, so the refund on the unexempted segment's 5.15 extra km is 5.15 × $1.41 = $7.26, which is the mileage-only amount RD-2 allows and is within the $8.35 excess-distance charge actually billed. [F4 F3] [RD-2]
C4: The driver's claimed reason — 'I followed my GPS; it rerouted me' — is not a justified cause under RD-4: no traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window, and the only speed records are band 4 (30–39 km/h) and band 5 (40–49 km/h), neither of which is band 1 or 2 severe congestion. [F9 F12 F10 F11] [RD-4]
C5: The rider never agreed to the reroute: the chat contains only the pickup greeting and the driver's arrival message, with no route-change proposal from the driver and no rider consent before the 12:12 off-route segment began, so no segment is exempt under RD-5. [F7 F8 F3] [RD-5]
C6: The driver has 2 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days (route: 2), and since this deviation is upheld here the case makes his conduct repeated, supporting an additional account review under RD-6; the profile record is offered only as support for that add-on action, not as proof of this deviation. [F15 F3] [RD-6]
C7: No waiting or stop charge was added for this trip ($0.00 waiting) and weather was fair, so no part of the extra mileage can be attributed to a rider-requested stop or to an excused condition under RD-3. [F6 F13] [RD-3]
Weaknesses: The driver will argue 'reasonable cause' for the reroute, pointing to the trip-window congestion records F10 (Ayer Rajah Expressway, band 4, 30–39 km/h) and F11 (Jurong Town Hall Road, band 5, 40–49 km/h); although neither is a band 1–2 record and F12 shows no incident, RD-4(b) leaves it to Ryde whether congestion bands alone can excuse a segment. | The rider has one dispute in 90 days with 0 upheld (F14), and the driver's 1093-trip record supports an alternative reading that he is a high-volume driver on a congested corridor — the profile facts F14/F15 cannot decide the case and cut for RD-6 only as an add-on. | The off-route segment only accounts for 5.15 km of the 5.9 km total excess (F1 vs F3); the remaining ~0.75 km is map-matching residual which RD-2 expressly does not refund, and the rider's complaint frames the whole 5.9 km as refundable, so the refund is necessarily partial, not full. | The driver's written statement F9 asserts the reroute came from his GPS navigation; if Ryde treats app-directed routing as a permissible route choice (Ryde's own guidance lets drivers take the fastest or most efficient GPS route), the deviation may be argued down even though no consent was obtained (F7, F8).
Asks: refund_partial $7.26

claims.assertion: The GPS track shows one off-route segment from 12:12 to 12:22 in which 6.47 km was driven where the optimal route covers 1.32 km, adding 5.15 km of extra distance and straying up to 1194 m from the optimal route; under RD-1 this unexplained deviation is a route deviation.

The trip was a RydeTAXI metered trip (total charged $31.56 by meter, distance $20.43 at 14.5 km), so the extra kilometres the driver drove enter the fare directly; RD-2 requires a partial refund of Σ(extra_km) × per-km rate for the non-exempt segment.

Using the fare facts for this trip, the per-kilometre rate is $1.41, so the refund on the unexempted segment's 5.15 extra km is 5.15 × $1.41 = $7.26, which is the mileage-only amount RD-2 allows and is within the $8.35 excess-distance charge actually billed.

The driver's claimed reason — 'I followed my GPS; it rerouted me' — is not a justified cause under RD-4: no traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window, and the only speed records are band 4 (30–39 km/h) and band 5 (40–49 km/h), neither of which is band 1 or 2 severe congestion.

The rider never agreed to the reroute: the chat contains only the pickup greeting and the driver's arrival message, with no route-change proposal from the driver and no rider consent before the 12:12 off-route segment began, so no segment is exempt under RD-5.

The driver has 2 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days (route: 2), and since this deviation is upheld here the case makes his conduct repeated, supporting an additional account review under RD-6; the profile record is offered only as support for that add-on action, not as proof of this deviation.

No waiting or stop charge was added for this trip ($0.00 waiting) and weather was fair, so no part of the extra mileage can be attributed to a rider-requested stop or to an excused condition under RD-3.

weaknesses: The driver will argue 'reasonable cause' for the reroute, pointing to the trip-window congestion records F10 (Ayer Rajah Expressway, band 4, 30–39 km/h) and F11 (Jurong Town Hall Road, band 5, 40–49 km/h); although neither is a band 1–2 record and F12 shows no incident, RD-4(b) leaves it to Ryde whether congestion bands alone can excuse a segment.

The rider has one dispute in 90 days with 0 upheld (F14), and the driver's 1093-trip record supports an alternative reading that he is a high-volume driver on a congested corridor — the profile facts F14/F15 cannot decide the case and cut for RD-6 only as an add-on.

The off-route segment only accounts for 5.15 km of the 5.9 km total excess (F1 vs F3); the remaining ~0.75 km is map-matching residual which RD-2 expressly does not refund, and the rider's complaint frames the whole 5.9 km as refundable, so the refund is necessarily partial, not full.

The driver's written statement F9 asserts the reroute came from his GPS navigation; if Ryde treats app-directed routing as a permissible route choice (Ryde's own guidance lets drivers take the fastest or most efficient GPS route), the deviation may be argued down even though no consent was obtained (F7, F8).

events.title: Driver Advocate brief: 10 claims (0 void)
events.body:
D1: The trip was a RydeTAXI metered job (F6), so any refund is limited to the mileage units of the unexplored off-route segment, computed as extra_km × (distance_fare ÷ distance_km), and not to the whole fare difference the rider demands. [F6 F4] [RD-2]
D2: Only one off-route segment exists — 12:12–12:22, 6.47 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.32 km, i.e. 5.15 km extra (F3) — and the remaining gap between the 5.9 km total excess (F1) and that segment is unattributed map-matching residue which is not refundable. [F3 F1] [RD-1 RD-2]
D3: Applying the taxi per-km rate of $1.41 (F4, F6) to the single off-route segment's 5.15 km extra gives $7.26 as the maximum distance-related exposure for my client on this trip. [F3 F4 F6] [RD-2]
D4: No traffic incident on the optimal route was recorded during the trip window (F12), so the reroute cannot be excused under the incident limb of the reasonable-cause exception. [F12] [RD-4]
D5: The only congestion records are speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) on the Ayer Rajah Expressway and band 5 (40–49 km/h) on Jurong Town Hall Road (F10, F11), both well above the band 1–2 severe-congestion range and therefore not sufficient to excuse the segment. [F10 F11] [RD-4]
D6: No chat message shows the rider requesting or naming an alternative stop or route before the deviation, and the driver's own statement offers only 'I followed my GPS; it rerouted me' (F7, F8, F9), so no consent-based exemption applies to the segment under RD-5. [F7 F8 F9] [RD-5]
D7: The waiting line on the bill is $0.00 (F6), so no waiting or stop-duration charge was taken and no fee_waived adjustment is required for the 12:12–12:22 period. [F6] [RD-3]
D8: No unpublished add-on appears in the breakdown — base $3.90, distance $20.43, time $5.76, platform $1.47, discount $0.00, no surge (F5, F6) — so the fare-schedule limb is not in dispute and only the metered mileage units remain. [F5 F6] [FARE-1]
D9: My client's 90-day record shows 2 route disputes, both upheld (F15); under RD-6 that profile alone cannot decide liability, and it should be weighed against a 3.4-year account with a 4.61 rating over 1093 trips (F15) and against the rider's own 1 dispute with 0 upheld (F14). [F14 F15] [RD-6]
D10: The rider's claim of '14 km charged' overstates a 14.5 km actual track (F1, F6), and the fare legitimately includes legitimate base, time and platform components (F6); only the off-route mileage units are refundable, giving a requested partial refund capped at $7.26. [F1 F3 F4 F6] [RD-2 FARE-1]
Weaknesses: The GPS record is squarely against my client: the off-route segment in F3 added 5.15 km and the total track was +69% over optimal (F1), with duration +8.4 min (F2) — the rider will lean on F1, F2 and F3 to establish an unexplained deviation under RD-1. | F12 records no traffic incident near the route, so my client cannot claim the incident-based reasonable-cause exemption (RD-4(a)); F10 and F11 show only band 4–5 speeds, which RD-4(b) does not treat as standalone justification. | The chat record (F7, F8, F9) contains no pre-deviation rider consent and no explanation from my client beyond 'I followed my GPS', which is exactly the situation RD-5 refuses to exempt. | My client's profile shows 2 upheld route disputes in 90 days (F15), which exposes him to an RD-6 flag_account referral even though the profile cannot itself decide this case.
Asks: refund_partial $7.26

Using the fare facts for this trip, the per-kilometre rate is $1.41, so the refund on the unexempted segment's 5.15 extra km is 5.15 × $1.41 = $7.26, which is the mileage-only amount RD-2 allows and is within the $8.35 excess-distance charge actually billed.

The rest of the extra mileage you mentioned is minor map-matching imprecision, which we do not refund. The driver's account is being referred to Ryde review for this upheld route deviation. Nothing further is needed from you.

Your fare dispute review is complete. One detour was recorded on this metered trip, between 12:12 and 12:22, where you drove about 6.47 km against a 1.32 km direct route. No rider-requested stop or reroute, waiting charge, incident, or severe congestion covered it, and a GPS reroute on its own is not an accepted reason. This is an upheld route deviation, so $7.26 of the mileage will be refunded to the rider as a Ryde voucher. Because this follows an earlier upheld deviation, your account is being referred to Ryde review. Continue accepting trips as normal.
